title: Integration tests: synthetic SLO breach harness + CI job (auto-rollback)
author: Leila Farouk
description: Motivation: As part of the auto-rollback on SLO breach project, we need an end-to-end test that proves the control plane can (1) consume monitors, (2) evaluate latency/error SLOs across an evaluation window with min-traffic + warm-up guardrails, and (3) execute a rollback deterministically. This PR adds a synthetic SLO breach integration test harness and wires it into CI so regressions are caught before rollout-controller changes ship. What changed: Adds an integration test suite that spins up a local rollout-controller (test config), a fake monitor backend implementing the monitor query contract (latency p95 + 5xx rate), and a minimal routing config store stub so we can verify traffic-split reverts on breach. The harness simulates baseline-good metrics, then injects a sustained breach (latency and/or error) while meeting min-traffic thresholds, and asserts: verdict transitions HEALTHY -> BREACHING, rollback executor is invoked exactly once (idempotency key), routing config is reverted to the prior stable version, and audit/event emission happens (captured via test sink). Also includes flake reduction: fake clock + deterministic window boundaries, explicit warm-up wait, and polling backoff tuned to avoid timing races in CI. CI: Adds a dedicated Buildkite job `integration:rollout_slo_breach` gated on changes under rollout-controller and policy evaluation modules; job runs the harness in a containerized env and uploads decision traces as artifacts on failure. Notes: Test suite is tagged `integration` and is excluded from default `go test ./...` to keep unit CI fast. Follow-ups: We still need a second scenario to cover monitor outage -> UNKNOWN verdict with fail-open vs fail-closed policy (tracked in ENG-2318/ENG-18546).
commits: test(rollout): add synthetic monitor backend + fixtures for latency/error time series
test(rollout): add e2e SLO breach -> rollback integration test (latency + 5xx)
test(rollout): stabilize timing with fake clock and deterministic evaluation windows
ci(buildkite): add integration job for rollout SLO breach harness + artifacts
docs(testing): note integration tags and local run instructions
files_changed: rollout-controller/README.md (update: integration test tag + env vars)
conversation: Miles Thornton (review): The core scenario looks right, but I’m worried about flapping due to timing jitter. Can we make the evaluation window boundaries deterministic and avoid using real wall clock sleeps?

Leila Farouk (author): Yep—good call. I pushed a follow-up commit that injects a fake clock into the evaluator and advances time explicitly to hit exact window cutovers. Also replaced the last `time.Sleep` with a harness-level barrier waiting for the first HEALTHY verdict before injecting the breach.

Benji Okafor (review): The harness stubs routing config store—can we assert we’re exercising the same traffic-split revert path as production (idempotency key + “prior stable” lookup), not a test-only shortcut?

Leila Farouk (author): Updated assertions to validate the executor call includes the real idempotency key format (rollout_id + policy_hash) and the routing revert writes the expected version pointer (stable_version) rather than overwriting canary directly. Also added a negative test that a second breach tick does not trigger a second revert.

Nadia Rahman (review): For the fake monitor server: please ensure we’re matching the monitor identity contract fields and not depending on legacy labels. This should fail loudly if labels are missing so we catch regressions like INT-3310.

Leila Farouk (author): Done—server now validates required labels (route, model, region, tier, slo_type) and returns a structured error; test asserts we emit monitor-fetch errors to the trace when identity is incomplete. Added a small fixture for the SUP-18457 scenario (stale/empty response) but left it as skipped pending UNKNOWN verdict semantics.
Sahana Iyer (review): CI runtime: initial numbers show ~11–13 minutes. Can we keep this under 8 minutes? Also we need retries configured; integration jobs are the first to flake in buildkite.

Leila Farouk (author): Reduced runtime by trimming the container image (removed unused tooling), lowering log verbosity, and tightening the polling interval with exponential backoff. Current runtime on CI is ~7m40s. Added a single retry on the step with artifact upload on failure so we can debug flakes if they occur.
Miles Thornton (approve): Looks solid. The fake clock change is exactly what we needed. Approving.
Benji Okafor (approve): +1. Thanks for validating executor idempotency behavior.
Nadia Rahman (approve): Identity checks look good; this should catch label regressions early.
Sahana Iyer (approve): CI changes are acceptable; please keep an eye on flake rate over the next week.
release_notes: Internal: add CI coverage for auto-rollback synthetic SLO breach scenario; reduces risk of regressions in evaluator/executor wiring.
